questionText:
Let $P(x)$ be an arbitrary predicate over the domain of natural numbers.

Which ONE of the following statements is TRUE?
explanation:
Step-by-step Explanation:

Step 1: Identify the Principle of Mathematical Induction.
The statement in Option (A) is the formal representation of the Principle of Mathematical Induction over the set of natural numbers $\mathbb{N} = \{0, 1, 2, \dots\}$.

• Base Case: $P(0)$ asserts that the predicate holds for $x = 0$.
• Inductive Step: $\forall x [P(x) \implies P(x + 1)]$ asserts that if the predicate holds for any natural number $x$, it must also hold for $x + 1$.
• Conclusion: Combining the base case and inductive step implies that $P(x)$ holds for all natural numbers, represented by $\forall x P(x)$.

Step 2: Analysis of other options.
• Option (B): Going backward ($P(x) \implies P(x - 1)$) from $0$ does not cover all positive natural numbers.
• Option (C): Starting at $1000$ and moving backward ($x - 1$) only covers values $0 \le x \le 1000$, not all natural numbers.
• Option (D): Starting at $1000$ and moving forward ($x + 1$) leaves natural numbers from $0$ to $999$ unverified.

Hence, Option (A) is the only logically true statement for all natural numbers.
